_readme: Which party held the seat that fell vacant, per by-election. HAND VERIFIED, never derived.
_why_not_derived: The obvious derivation, take the winner of the ward's last ordinary election, is wrong wherever a ward returns more than one councillor. Sheffield Southey is the worked example: a three-member ward elected by thirds, Reform UK won the seat contested in May 2026, and the seat that fell vacant in July belonged to an independent. Deriving it would have published 'Reform hold' for a contest that is a Reform gain if they win it. Gains and holds are the whole story of local by-elections, so a wrong one is worse than none: contests absent from this file are shown as not established rather than assumed.
_requirements: Every entry needs at least two independent sources, and the party is the one the member sat for AT THE MOMENT THE SEAT FELL VACANT, which is not always the one they were elected under. Defections are common and are the reason this field exists.

local.sheffield.southey.by.2026-08-27.note: Elected as Labour, left the party to sit as an independent, then resigned in July 2026 citing family commitments. The seat is therefore defended by nobody in practice: no independent is standing. Reform UK holds a different Southey seat, won in May 2026, so a Reform win here is a gain and not a hold.
local.sheffield.southey.by.2026-08-27.vacated_day_disputed: Reported as 1 July by the Sheffield Star and 2 July by Wikipedia. The day is not published here because the two sources disagree and nothing turns on it.
